svg.title: Impulse Response vs Forecast Error Variance Decomposition
svg.desc: IRF shows how a shock spreads over time; FEVD shows which shock explains how much of the forecast error variance. Both depend on identification.
svg.text: How a shock spreads vs who explains how much of the forecast error
Response curves per variable and shock
bottoms out about six months later
How shares shift with the horizon
Also needs to be read with bands
In the long run 40% of output variance
Response path to a single shock
Read when it crosses zero and when it dies out
Contribution by horizon — always sums to 100%
The longer the horizon, the larger the share of other shocks
For variables in levels, the cumulative response is the permanent effect
Same data, different ordering — the conclusion changes
Choose the ordering on economic grounds and report the sensitivity
IRF shows the path of a shock; FEVD shows the share of variance that path creates.
Both come from the same MA coefficients, so they are a pair with one shared dependence on identification.
neither IRF nor FEVD can be interpreted
Read with the VECM and workflow sheets to complete the path from estimation to interpretation.
